wstep: This card describes NCHFP tomato juice, hot packed and processed in a boiling-water bath with added acid.

akapity: According to an FDA list, tomatoes have an approximate pH of 4.30–4.90, and the value varies widely with variety and conditions.
Sugar may be added to balance the acidic taste, but the acid must not be left out.
Add 2 tablespoons of bottled lemon juice or 1/2 teaspoon of citric acid per quart jar (about 0.95 l) of juice.
For pint jars, use 1 tablespoon of bottled lemon juice or 1/4 teaspoon of citric acid.
Do not can tomatoes from dead or frost-killed vines.
Add the bottled lemon juice or citric acid to the jars, heat the juice to boiling again and fill the jars with hot juice, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace.
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) above sea level, process the juice in a boiling-water bath for 35 minutes in pint jars and 40 minutes in quart jars.
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased.
At 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m) process pints for 40 minutes and quarts for 45.
At 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m) process pints for 45 minutes and quarts for 50.
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process pints for 50 minutes and quarts for 55.
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m.
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage.
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml.
For a jar of up to 473 ml use the pint time, and for a larger jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, use the quart time.
NCHFP gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so use smaller jars.
